thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Futures Tumble More Than 250 Points On Jobs Day

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Futures Tumble More Than 250 Points On Jobs Day
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Dow, S&P 500 face worst weekly performances since late 2016
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures sank more than 250 points on Friday, as global government bond yields continued to climb, and investors braced for an important U.S. jobs update.
Premarket gains for Apple Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. provided a bright spot after those companies delivered upbeat results, but appeared unable to do lift the main indexes that are now facing their worst weekly performance in more than a year.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures tumbled 257 points, or 1%, to 25,915, while S&P 500 futures slid 23.15 points, or 0.8%, to 2,799.50. Nasdaq-100 futures slumped 33 points, or 0.5%, to 6,865.25.
Rising bond yields and concerns about higher inflation left stocks mostly lower on Thursday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sp-500-poised-to-rise-lifted-by-ebay-surge-2018-02-01). The Dow Jones Industrial Average was an exception, rising 37.32 points, or 0.1%, to finish at 26,186.71, after shaking off a 135-point loss at one point in the session. The S&P 500 index slipped 0.1% to end at 2,821.98, while the Nasdaq Composite Index slid 25.62 points, or 0.4%, at 7,385.86.
A couple of bruising sessions this week have left their mark. The S&P 500 was down 1.8% on the week as of Thursday's close, set for its worst weekly performance since November 2016. The Dow average was facing a 1.6% weekly loss, its worst since September 2016. The Nasdaq Composite, meanwhile, was looking at a 1.6% loss, the deepest seen since last June.
What are strategists saying?
"Stock traders are not happy to see that the multi-month rallies they've enjoyed are now under threat but we believe we're still far away from this correction turning into a broader sell off," said Konstantinos Anthis, on the research team at ADS Securities, in a note to clients.
 in Amazon Inc.(AMZN) climbed 5.7% in thin premarket trading after the e-commerce retailer posted fourth-quarter profit and revenue that blew past forecasts.

Apple Inc. shares (AAPL) rose 1.7% in premarket, after the iPhone maker reported record earnings thanks to sales of the iPhone X, though its forecast fell short of expectations. As well, the company said it plans to spend some of its enormous cash pile.
See:Live-blog recap of Apple results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-to-focus-on-iphone-x-sales-live-blog-2018-02-01)

Google-parent Alphabet Inc.(GOOGL) slid 3.5% ahead of the open, after missing forecasts for fourth-quarter earnings. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/alphabet-shares-plunge-after-fourth-quarter-earnings-2018-02-01)
Read: Google earnings: Cloud is a $1 billion business, execs say (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/google-earnings-cloud-is-a-1-billion-business-execs-say-2018-02-01)
Mattel Inc.(MAT) plunged 6.7% in premarket action after the toy maker posted a steep sales decline during its important holiday period. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mattel-shares-tumble-after-weak-holiday-quarter-2018-02-01)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mattel-shares-tumble-after-weak-holiday-quarter-2018-02-01)U.S.-listed shares of Deutsche Bank AG(DBK.XE) slid 6.6%, echoing a loss in Frankfurt, after the German bank posted a $2.7 billion loss, owing to the U.S. tax overhaul (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/deutsche-bank-dragged-to-loss-by-us-tax-hit-2018-02-02).
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/deutsche-bank-dragged-to-loss-by-us-tax-hit-2018-02-02)Ahead of Friday's open, earnings from Merck & Co.(MRK) , Phillips 66 (PSX) and J.C. Penney Co.(JCP) are all on the docket.
What could help drive markets?
Stocks were taking a hit as global government bond yields, which have dogged stocks this week, continued to climb on Friday. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note rose to 2.8%.
Meanwhile, the yield on 10-year German government bunds added 4 basis points to reach 0.690%, close to levels not seen in more than two years. Higher returns on debt securities tend to weaken appetite for stocks and other assets perceived as risky.
Investors have been waiting all week for nonfarm payrolls data for January, due at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, with economists polled by MarketWatch forecasting a gain of 185,000. The unemployment rate, which economists see holding steady at 4.1%, and average hourly earnings, expected to creep up 0.2%, are due at the same time.
Read: U.S. jobs report in January likely to show meaty gain in hiring, low unemployment (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/january-jobs-bonanza-hiring-likely-rebounded-in-early-2018-2018-02-01)
(http://www.marketwatch.com/story/january-jobs-bonanza-hiring-likely-rebounded-in-early-2018-2018-02-01)Plus:A new report says the unemployment rate may have a lot more room to fall (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/back-to-the-1950s-a-new-report-says-the-unemployment-rate-may-have-a-lot-more-room-to-fall-2018-02-01)
Consumer sentiment for January is due at 10 a.m. Eastern, along with factory orders for December.
What are other assets doing?
European stocks slumped, driven by a 1.3% slide for the German DAX (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dax-drops-below-13000-after-deutsche-bank-logs-a-hefty-loss-2018-02-02) , in part dogged by Deutsche Bank's hefty loss. Asian markets saw a mixed session, with the Nikkei 225 index down 0.9% on disappointing earnings. Gold was flat, while oil futures inched up, and the ICE U.S. Dollar Index rose.
